source: cargo run -q -p lp-emu-esp32c6 --release -- --elf target/emu-ref/735af98ae-esp32c6+server+radio/fw-esp32c6 --time-grade t1 --usb-sj file:target/validate/boot-idle-flash.cap --usb-sj-tried file:target/validate/boot-idle-flash.tried --usb-host attached --timeout 16s --wall-timeout 320 --strict-bus --exit-on '[stack] heartbeat: high-water' --efuse-mac a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c --efuse-rev 0.2
note: running the pinned image target/emu-ref/735af98ae-esp32c6+server+radio/fw-esp32c6 rather than building one. It is the shipped image over its own USB-Serial-JTAG link — no `spike_uart0_link`, no cherry-pick — so that it is the same bytes a silicon flash of the same commit puts on the board, which is what makes a memory comparison a comparison of two machines rather than of two link drivers (DD30). `scripts/emu/build-reference-image.sh esp32c6,server,radio <commit> none` builds it in a detached worktree at that commit.

trust.because: the allocator is the guest's own and the RAM model is byte-exact, and on the compile harness this configuration is byte-equal to silicon — 372/372 values, peak 48,132 / resident 18,932 / after-drop 3,976 B and all 184 per-tick figures (M3 P6). That is evidence, not a promotion: the boot-idle heap sample sits 104 B below esp-emu's §5.4 figure (266,688 vs 266,792 at 5 s; 266,788 by 15 s, 4 B away), a transient in silent guest state that only a silicon capture of the memfs variant can arbitrate. Never tuned toward it

t1 counts one cycle per instruction — no cache, no flash wait states — and neither grade is graded by a transcript yet (the vision's 'time is a graded ladder, never a promise'). What is modelled honestly is the UART drain, at baud in emulated time, which is why the harness's log-bearing ticks land at 1.01x silicon while its compute ticks are 0.42x

there is no boot log: a direct load places the app's segments and jumps to its entry, so no ROM banner and no IDF bootloader lines are printed at all. M7 boots from reset and is where this class becomes a claim

M6 built the host's side — absent, attached with the port closed, attached and draining — and four committed transcripts under `lp-emu/transcripts/esp32c6/` are what it has to show for it: `boot-idle` over the shipped link against sitting 1's silicon capture of the SAME image bytes (stack high-water 11,784 B equal, heap 8 B apart); `usb-negative-control`, the port held closed from boot and opened at eight seconds, latching at 893 ms and recovering at 8,145; `usb-detach-reattach`, the cable out at six seconds and back at nine, recovering with exactly one hello and the firmware noticing nothing; and `usb-host-absent`, where the stamp pair reads 893 / never — the discriminator absent-vs-unread. The block's own registers are graded one by one (`--strict-grade`, the table in `periph/usb_sj.rs`) and the data path is `measured` there. This class stays `modeled` all the same, by the rule the ADR states and DD33 Q4 confirmed: byte-equality and agreement are EVIDENCE, weighed here where a reader can see them, not a promotion. What earns `measured` is a silicon transcript of this class, and the one M6 needs — `usb-negative-control` on the desk board — is owed

no pin is observed: GPIO and IO_MUX accept and remember; the RMT TX engines (M5 P1) produce each channel's pulses in cycles, but no pad carries them and nothing decodes them. M5 P2 brings the signal fabric, the pin log and the WS281x decoder that make a pin claim possible

the bytes are the guest's own, drained through a UART0 model at the configured baud, so their content and order are the firmware's. What is not the firmware's is when a host's bytes arrive on a live socket — that is host time, not guest time, and `--uart0-script` is the deterministic path for anything a transcript should carry
